the oxidation of some perfluorocyclopentanes and perfluorocyclotetraenes and the oxidation of perfluorocarbonyl compounds.
the chemistry of the Cw CO 2 laser, which has been applied to the oxidation of some perfluorinated and perhalogenated cycloalkenes.

Cw CO 2 laser photolysis of the perhalogenocarbocyclic compounds studied in this work leads to a variety of reactions, including the oxidation of the parent compounds, the retro-Diels–Alder cleavage of decafluorcyclohexene, the decomposition of oxalate esters into oxalyl halide and halogen and the decomposition of oxaly fluoride into carbon dioxide and COF 2.
the title reaction is not a general oxidation of perhalogenocarbons, rather it represents a special case of the oxidation of cyclobutene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perfluorocyclopentenes are more resistant against CO 2 laser induced oxidation than the perfluorinated cyclobutenes and the cyclohexenes.

the oxidation of the title perhalogenocyclic hydrocarbons proceeds through an initial formation of the corresponding perhalogenocarboxylic acids, which then decompose into COX and CO, and that the oxidation of perhalogenocarbon acids is favored over the oxidation of the parent hydrocarbons, which is in agreement with the general trend that the oxidation of organic compounds proceeds through their oxidation products.
Cw CO 2 laser driven reactions of organic compounds are not only useful for the study of reaction kinetics but also as a tool for preparative chemistry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CO 2 laser is a very efficient source of energy for driving oxidation of halocarbon molecules.
the oxidation of the perhalocycloalkene precursors is a viable route to oxalyl halide and COF 2 formation.
the oxidation of perhalogenocarboxylic acids is a more effective method of producing CO 2 from CO 2 than the oxidation of the corresponding perhalogenoalkanes.
